name: sidebar-item
description: One entry in a sidebar list (sidebar-list composes several). type="set": one row of a sets sidebar (a clickable name, optional save toggle). type="card": a subtitle, a saved-icon, a title and a status line. type="button": a single primary action. Renamed from Penpot's "Sidebar" to avoid colliding with the composed list, which this system names sidebar-list.

props.name: type
props.description: "card" renders the subtitle/title/status card (Penpot's Default/PDF Downloaded/Submitted States -- identical layout, only the status text differs, so not modeled as three separate types); "button" renders a single centered .ds-text-button instead (Penpot's own "Button" State) -- not a card at all. "set" (not from Penpot, see rationale) renders a clickable set-name button + toggleable save icon on one row, one caption line below.

props.name: name
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". The set's name, rendered as a clickable secondary text-button (selects the set), truncated with an ellipsis when it overflows.

props.name: caption
props.description: type="set": optional second line under the name, in grey (text-active at half opacity, the same grey as table-cell's text-passive-cell) -- e.g. a record's status. The row grows to two lines; without it the set row stays the single 44px line. (Kept from the earlier Penpot set card; shown again since 2026-09-30.)

props.name: saved
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". Initial data-saved state for the save icon; component.js keeps it in sync on click and dispatches ds-sidebar-item-favourite-toggle.

props.name: active
props.description: type="set": marks the active set (fill and hairlines above and below).

props.name: href
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". When given, the set name renders as an <a href> (still the same secondary/dotted text-button) instead of a <button data-select-set> -- for a sidebar whose rows navigate, e.g. an in-page section index (dotted, because it stays on the page; CLAUDE.md, Interaction conventions). Passed through the safe_url filter.

props.name: save
props.description: Only meaningful when type="set". false omits the save button entirely (a navigation row has nothing to save). Default true.

rationale:
type="set" (Figma sets sidebar): a 44px row with the set's name as a text button and a 44px save button with Figma's bookmark icons (aria-pressed toggles them); the active set (data-active) is filled and ruled above and below, and its name uses the body-text medium weight, so the current set stands out without a new type scale. The saved icon is accent-1, the same as table-cell's row-level favourite: one save flag, one color, wherever it renders. With `href`, the name renders as an <a> (navigation, e.g. an in-page section index) instead of a <button>, and save=false omits the save button; one row layout serves both uses. Rows deviate from text-button's hover brackets: on hover and focus the whole row takes bg.surface-pressed, as table-row does, and the name gets no brackets -- the full-width fill already marks the click target. The dotted underline stays. A long name truncates with an ellipsis (the composed text button can shrink: flex 1 1 auto, min-width 0).

type="card" and type="button" (Penpot "Sidebar" states Default, PDF Downloaded, Submitted, Button): the main section is a space-between row and the sub section a column with rowGap spacing-3, both Token-bound in Penpot. Card padding is spacing-2 / spacing-5. Colors are read off the text layers: subtitle accent-1 (the one colored identifier a reader scans the list for), title text-active, status text-subactive. The saved icon is object-dark-active at spacing-7 (24px), like every other icon-only glyph. Width is 100%, because a sidebar's width comes from its container, not from Penpot's 340px demo board. type="button" is shorter (70px vs 84px) and centered, holding one primary text-button, as Penpot's own instance is. Selecting, linking or adding records is the host application's concern. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: type="set": the name is a real <button> (or <a> with href; the active row gets aria-current), and the save control is a real <button> with aria-pressed and an aria-label naming the set, so both are keyboard-operable. type="card": the saved-icon is a decorative role="img" span with an aria-label, not a control -- the design shows no affordance on it. type="button" is a real <button> via text-button.
